title: A multi-layer portfolio design for reducing crop-concentration risk
research_question: Under climate and pest shocks, when do rotations, intercropping, cultivar mixtures, habitat, and neglected crops improve delivered food stability and ecosystem services without unacceptable yield, income, nutrition, land, water, or labour penalties?
interventions: neglected or underutilized crop transition corridors

stages.name: baseline_and_historical_risk
stages.purpose: Estimate concentration, covariance, tail loss, recovery, and value-chain bottlenecks from harmonized observations.

stages.name: controlled_field_experiments
stages.purpose: Randomize portfolio components and measure agronomic, ecological, and resource mechanisms across sites and seasons.

stages.name: farm_and_value_chain_trials
stages.purpose: Measure income, labour, machinery, storage, processing, price, and adoption persistence under real operating constraints.

stages.name: shock_experiments_and_simulation
stages.purpose: Stress-test portfolios against observed and counterfactual compound heat, drought, flood, and pest-pathogen scenarios.

stages.name: adoption_and_policy
stages.purpose: Estimate how seed, insurance, procurement, infrastructure, and incentives change feasible adoption.

stages.name: out_of_sample_validation
stages.purpose: Evaluate transfer across regions, farm sizes, seasons, and shocks not used for calibration.

estimands: average treatment effect of each portfolio component
cost per unit reduction in lower-tail delivered nutrition loss
risk-adjusted income effect and adoption threshold

model.multiobjective_vector: J(P,r)=[food, income, resilience, soil, biodiversity, water, GHG, labour, adoption]

safety_and_governance: follow phytosanitary rules for seed movement
screen neglected crops for food safety and anti-nutritional factors
protect participating farms from uncompensated downside risk
pre-register primary estimands and report null and adverse effects
limitations: rare shocks require long panels or calibrated scenarios
portfolio performance can be displaced through land-use change
food-system concentration may persist after field diversification
nutritional equivalence requires processing and consumption data
